name: Reaching Families Who Are Hardest to Reach
title: Reaching Families Who Are Hardest to Reach
answer: Reaching families who are hardest to reach means checking whether messages actually arrive and then using other contact methods when they do not. The idea matters because the families schools most need to reach are often the least likely to receive the messages schools send. AI can help identify which families need outreach, but people make the contact.

sections.body: The problem is that schools often rely on messaging platforms and assume contact happens, while the families with the greatest needs may be the least likely to receive those messages. Phone numbers change, email addresses go unchecked, and some families do not use the apps schools prefer. A message that never arrives cannot help, so delivery and read reports need to be checked by school and by language. Families who never open messages may need a phone call, a home visit, or a note sent home with the child. AI can help identify which families to reach out to, and people make the contact.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, schools can use the delivery and read reports that most messaging platforms provide, breaking them out by school and language to see who is actually receiving messages. Contact information should be updated regularly, not only at enrollment, and a short reminder each semester can ask families to confirm their phone number and preferred language. Families should be able to choose how they want to be reached, because meeting families where they are works better than expecting them to use the school's preferred channel. The text does not give grade band examples, so this practice applies across grade levels. When families never open messages, staff can follow up with a phone call, a home visit, or a note sent home with the child.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text cites a trial using existing messaging platforms, Musaddiq et al., 2023, which found that the neediest parents were the least likely to receive messages. The text does not give a separate evidence label, a figure, or additional findings. Beyond that cited trial, the idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text warns that some families distrust messages from institutions, sometimes for good reason, and that immigrant families may worry about how their information is used, especially in times of heightened immigration enforcement. Schools should explain clearly what information they collect and why. Trust grows slowly, through consistent, honest, and respectful communication. The decisions about who to contact and how to contact them stay with people, even when AI helps identify which families to reach out to. The text does not set out legal rules or consent requirements, so these are practice considerations rather than legal advice.
